children: CEO Justin Hotard says the AI infrastructure boom is being constrained more by supply than by demand, arguing that data centers could be built roughly twice as fast if bottlenecks disappeared. For investors, the comments strengthen Nokia's emerging position as a picks-and-shovels beneficiary of AI spending while shifting attention toward whether the company can convert surging orders into revenue fast enough.

Nokia supplies networking equipment across optical, IP, fixed and mobile infrastructure, with increasing exposure to hyperscalers and AI data centers. Its opportunity has expanded as large computing clusters require faster networking between servers and facilities.

I don't think you can say in any manner we're overbuilding today because reality is that if we could build 2x faster, our customers could build 2x faster, they probably would, Hotard said. So that gives me confidence that we're still in the early days of the AI buildout.

That confidence is already showing up in Nokia's results. Second-quarter AI & Cloud order intake reached 2.8 billion, while sales to AI and cloud customers more than doubled year over year. Nokia said roughly half of those orders should convert into revenue within 12 months, while supply remains the industry's main constraint.

Network Infrastructure sales rose 12% year over year in the second quarter, helped by 20% growth in Optical Networks and 16% growth in IP Networks. Nokia currently expects full-year comparable operating profit of 2.1 billion to 2.6 billion.
Hotard also argued that AI demand does not depend solely on ever-more-powerful frontier models.
Even if we didn't have another frontier model released in the next three years, we could probably make tremendous progress just deploying the technology that's there today.

The next test comes on October 22, when Nokia reports third-quarter results. Investors should focus on AI & Cloud order intake, Optical and IP Networks growth, backlog conversion and whether supply constraints ease.

The bullish case strengthens if hyperscaler spending keeps translating into double-digit Network Infrastructure growth and improving margins. The main risk is that Nokia's roughly 130% one-year stock rally has already priced in substantial AI upside, leaving the shares more exposed if orders slow, supply bottlenecks persist or data-center capital spending cools.

title: Nokia CEO Issues Bold AI Verdict as Industry Stakes Rise
